nodes.name: Schedule Trigger
nodes.notes: Polls for pending broadcasts every 25s. Replaces the original Webhook-trigger design after n8n's production webhook registration was found to be broken in this deployment — confirmed across three n8n versions (2.33.7, 1.123.69, 1.70.0), via CLI activation, genuine UI clicks, full-body PATCH, and container restarts; workflows showed active=true with a correct webhook_entity row, but the production URL always 404'd. Schedule Trigger uses n8n's internal scheduler, a structurally different and far more battle-tested code path, unaffected by that bug. admin-gui now INSERTs directly into `broadcasts` (status='pending') instead of calling a webhook — see admin-gui/server.js's POST /api/broadcast.

nodes.name: Claim Next Pending Broadcast
nodes.notes: Atomically claims the oldest pending broadcast with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so two overlapping poll executions (e.g. a slow prior run still finishing when the next tick fires) can never claim the same row and double-send. Calls claim_next_pending_broadcast() (db/migrations/012_rls_helper_functions.sql), which sets the RLS branch context via set_config and runs the claim inside one PL/pgSQL function body — a WITH-CTE version of this was tried first and does NOT work: an unreferenced CTE never executes at all, and even referenced, the planner can evaluate RLS's USING clause before it since both are just ANDed quals with no ordering guarantee (confirmed by direct testing, not a hypothetical). Sequential statements inside a single PL/pgSQL function are the only ordering Postgres actually guarantees. 'ALL' is used unconditionally for now since only one branch exists and admin-gui doesn't yet support branch selection (see docs/MIGRATION.md's National rollout section for when this needs to become per-branch).

nodes.name: Fetch Sender Profile
nodes.notes: Keyed directly by sender_profile_id (a UUID already resolved when admin-gui inserted the broadcasts row) rather than (branch_slug, role) — simpler now that there's no webhook body to parse role strings out of. Runs once (single input item), so its output is safely available to every later node via $('Fetch Sender Profile').first().json, including inside the Batch Members loop.

nodes.name: Data Source Router
nodes.notes: DATA_SOURCE env var controls Phase 1 (sheets) vs Phase 2+ (postgres). Postgres is the path tested in this repo; sheets requires a live Google OAuth2 credential and is unverified.

nodes.name: Fetch Members (Postgres)
nodes.notes: Filters by branch_id (a real UUID from the claimed broadcast row) directly, rather than joining through branches.slug — no slug is available anymore since there's no webhook body.

nodes.name: Fetch Members (Sheets)
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED: no live Google account was available to test this node. Column mapping assumes the Phase-1 sheet header row exactly matches docs/samples/nba_members_template.csv (First_Name, Last_Name, Email, Phone_Number, Financial_Status). Configure documentId/sheetName and the Google Sheets OAuth2 credential after import, then re-verify field names against a real spreadsheet.

nodes.name: Batch Members
nodes.notes: Output 0 (done) fires once after every batch has looped through; output 1 (loop) fires per batch and feeds the per-member send pipeline, which loops back into this node's input via the Wait node.

nodes.name: Select SMS Route
nodes.notes: is_urgent (legal/emergency notices) sets Multitexter's forcednd=1 to bypass Nigerian DND opt-outs; forcednd=0 otherwise. Confirmed against Multitexter's public API docs (https://www.multitexter.com/developers) and a real successful test send.

nodes.name: Channel: Email?
nodes.notes: Uses a plain boolean expression (.includes()) rather than the IF node's built-in 'array contains' operator with strict type validation — confirmed by a real local n8n execution that the built-in operator throws 'Wrong type: X is a string but was expecting an array' against a genuinely real, correctly-typed array (verified independently via node-postgres: dataTypeID 1009, Array.isArray() true) when that array has exactly one element. Not related to the RLS fix — a pre-existing n8n node quirk that only surfaces on real execution, never caught by this session's earlier Code-node-only unit tests.

nodes.name: Channel: WhatsApp?
nodes.notes: See Channel: Email?'s notes — same fix, same reason (the IF node's built-in 'array contains' operator misbehaves on a genuinely real single-element array).

nodes.name: Channel: SMS?
nodes.notes: See Channel: Email?'s notes — same fix, same reason (the IF node's built-in 'array contains' operator misbehaves on a genuinely real single-element array).

nodes.name: Send via Brevo Email
nodes.notes: Confirmed working by a real test send on 2026-08-09 (real messageId returned, HTTP 201, delivered to a live inbox). Endpoint/body shape per developers.brevo.com/reference/sendtransacemail. Subject now uses sender_display_name (e.g. 'Barr. Chukwuemeka Okafor, Branch Chairman') rather than the raw role string, since there's no webhook body carrying that string anymore.

nodes.name: Send via Sendchamp WhatsApp
nodes.notes: Reverted from Brevo: Brevo's WhatsApp product isn't available on its free tier. Sendchamp already has a tested API key from this session (auth confirmed working — its email/SMS test calls reached the account correctly) and its WhatsApp endpoint only failed on 'unable to get sender number', not a plan/billing wall — connect a WhatsApp Business number in Sendchamp's dashboard (see docs/PROVIDERS_SETUP.md) to get further. Interactive RSVP/payment buttons still require a Meta-approved WhatsApp template regardless of provider. custom_data param mapping is UNVERIFIED (built from Sendchamp's public docs only).

nodes.name: Send via Multitexter SMS
nodes.notes: Confirmed working by a real test send on 2026-08-08 (real msgid/messages returned, HTTP 200, delivered to a live phone). Multitexter authenticates with account email+password IN the JSON body (no header/token auth), so this node uses authentication: none and reads MULTITEXTER_EMAIL/MULTITEXTER_PASSWORD from env instead of an n8n credential.

nodes.name: Normalize Delivery Response (Email)
nodes.notes: Brevo returns HTTP 201 with a top-level messageId on success (confirmed by a real test send); on failure it returns an error body with no messageId. n8n's HTTP Request node surfaces the parsed body here regardless of status code, so presence of messageId is the success signal.

nodes.name: Normalize Delivery Response (WhatsApp)
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED: field names for Sendchamp's success indicator and message id are inferred from public docs; confirm against a real response (once a WhatsApp sender is connected) before relying on delivery status.

nodes.name: Normalize Delivery Response (SMS)
nodes.notes: Response shape confirmed against a real send on 2026-08-08: {status: 1, msgid, units, balance, msg, messages: {"<phone-without-plus>": "<per-recipient-message-id>"}}. status is a NUMBER (1 = success); a failure shape wasn't observed, so the ok-check falls back to treating any non-1 status as failure.

nodes.name: Insert Message Log
nodes.notes: Runs once per input item, i.e. once per (member, channel) pair — exactly the message_log grain.

nodes.name: Wait
nodes.notes: Throttles batch-to-batch pacing against Brevo/Sendchamp/Multitexter rate limits before looping back to Batch Members.

nodes.name: Update Broadcast Status
nodes.notes: Terminal node — there is no inbound HTTP request to respond to anymore (the old Respond to Admin GUI node is gone), admin-gui instead polls/queries broadcasts.status directly if it needs to show progress.
